module purpose: neorv32_neoled is a bus-accessible serial-output engine. Bus writes configure enable, format, interrupt and timing registers or enqueue 32-bit transmit words into a FIFO; the serial engine dequeues them, generates timed output on neoled_o from a selected clkgen_i tap, raises irq_o from FIFO level, and reports control/status on the bus response.

use-case flows.value: control-register settings for enable, frame format, interrupt mode and pulse timing
a transmit-buffer write request and the packed FIFO entry made from strobe, mode and bus data
dequeued FIFO entries loaded into the serial engine, shifted and timed into output pulses on neoled_o
interrupt request generated from the enabled FIFO-level condition
stored control settings and FIFO/engine status returned on bus_rsp_o.data
control registers, IRQ, serial state and output forced to zero when rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow stores ctrl.enable from the control write at line 130, then the module uses that held bit to drive clkgen_en_o (line 160), clear the FIFO when disabled (line 193), gate irq_o (line 201), and force the serial engine active bit in serial.state(2) (line 231). Corrupting this setting changes whether transmission resources run at all; availability is also established because the register is held between writes and reset by lines 112 and 130.

conceptual assets.concept: Transmission timing and default frame-format configuration
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow stores ctrl.mode, ctrl.strobe, ctrl.clk_prsc, ctrl.t_total, ctrl.t0_high and ctrl.t1_high at lines 131-137. These settings are then consumed to annotate FIFO entries (line 192), select the pulse source from clkgen_i (line 225), choose the current high-time for a 0 or 1 bit (lines 261 and 263), and end each bit or strobe period (lines 285 and 295). If these held values are corrupted, the generated frame width, optional strobe behavior, or pulse timing becomes wrong; availability is also established because the registers retain their values between writes and reset.

The configure flow stores ctrl.irq_conf at line 134 and reports it on reads at line 144. The irq_generator then uses that held setting to choose which FIFO condition can raise the interrupt: not tx_fifo.avail when ctrl.irq_conf is 0 (line 202) or not tx_fifo.half when ctrl.irq_conf is 1 (line 203). Corrupting this stored mode changes the implemented interrupt condition; availability is also established because the setting is held between writes and reset.

irq_o is registered from the boolean at lines 201-203: ctrl.enable and either not tx_fifo.avail or not tx_fifo.half, selected by ctrl.irq_conf. Integrity requires the external consumer of irq_o to receive exactly that request, and availability is established because irq_o updates on clk_i and resets low at line 199.

conceptual assets.concept: FIFO enqueue decision for a transmit-data write
conceptual assets.reasoning: The start flow computes tx_fifo.we at line 191 only when bus_req_i.stb is 1, bus_req_i.rw is 1 and bus_req_i.addr(2) is 1, and delivers that decision to the FIFO sub-block at line 182. Corrupting this decision would accept a write when the implemented predicate is false or miss one when it is true; availability is also established because, when the predicate holds, the request is passed to the FIFO consumer defined by the connection.

conceptual assets.concept: Transmission frame data and per-frame options
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module computes a FIFO entry as ctrl.strobe & ctrl.mode & bus_req_i.data at line 192 and sends it to data_buffer.wdata_i at line 181. On dequeue, tx_fifo.rdata drives serial.sreg with bits 31 downto 0 (line 239), selects serial.mode and serial.bit_cnt from bit 32 (lines 240-245), and selects the next serial.state low bits from bit 33 (lines 247-251). Integrity is established because the transmitted bits, frame length and optional strobe phase are taken from these values; availability is established because the value is buffered and then loaded when the engine reaches its load state. tx_fifo.rdata is not treated as mere sub-unit wiring here because its bits are locally tested at lines 240 and 248.

The serial engine keeps and updates its progress in serial.state, serial.bit_cnt, serial.pulse_clk, serial.pulse_cnt, serial.strobe_cnt and serial.t_high across lines 225, 231-232, 257-299 and 303-305, and derives serial.busy from serial.state at line 321 for status reporting at line 153. Integrity is established because these values define sequencing, remaining bits, pulse timing, strobe completion and busy indication; availability is also established because they are clocked state that is preserved and advanced under the RTL conditions.

The operate flow drives neoled_o low when loading or idle (lines 236 and 310), low on completion of a frame bit (line 266), high while transmitting a bit pulse (line 270), and low again when serial.pulse_cnt reaches serial.t_high during the timed high phase (line 282). Integrity is established because the external consumer of neoled_o depends on the exact generated level sequence, and availability is established when the engine is enabled and its progress state advances.
